fd47a768-1c13-5b0f-82f0-572eb14c0584.name: Benedictine Abbey of St. Theodor and St. Alexander
fd47a768-1c13-5b0f-82f0-572eb14c0584.description: The monastery complex designed by Father Christoph Vogt is not built facing east as is common, but rather, appears as a rectangle stretched from south to north and is divided in the same direction by a middle axis. In this way the combination of a Benedictine abbey cloister and a sovereign imperial foundation is given a special architectonic expression. The duality shown with the eastern half as a monastery divided by the library wing into two equal courtyards, and the western half surrounding a single courtyard with an outward projecting main facade as a secular, princely residence building, simultaneously appears included and preserved due to the framing effect of the quadrant construction. The abbey church stands alone in front of the north wing and the choir connects to the monastery complex. Its facade with pompous columns and high towers is intended to be viewed from afar. Inside, the colossal columns and pillars intensify the perspective view, the focus of which is the high altar.
fd47a768-1c13-5b0f-82f0-572eb14c0584.short_description: The Benedictine Abbey Ottobeuren, dominated by its massive Late Baroque church with delicate Rococo interior, belongs to the largest and most marvellous Baroque monastery complex of southern Germany. The former imperial abbey, often called the “Swabian Escorial”, has always been a centre of science and culture culminating in its representative Imperial Hall, which lives up to expectations, with an amazing display of splendour.
fd47a768-1c13-5b0f-82f0-572eb14c0584.dates: 1711–1731: monastery building; 1717–1724: economy building; 1737–1766: church; 1739–1740: government building
fd47a768-1c13-5b0f-82f0-572eb14c0584.method_for_datation: Archival documents, among which the diary of the 52nd abbot of Ottobeuren, Rupert Ness.
fd47a768-1c13-5b0f-82f0-572eb14c0584.bibliography:
Jahn, P. H., “Wenigst habe in Wien und Rom davon alle Ehr. Die 'kaiserliche' Phase in der Baupolitik des Reichsstiftes Ottobeuren”, *Zeitschrift für Kunstgeschicht*e, 67: 2, 2004, pp. 183–200.  
Hofer, S., *Studien zur Stuckausstattung im frühen 18. Jahrhundert. Modi und ihre Funktion in der Herrschaftsarchitektur am Beispiel Ottobeuren* (Kunstwissenschaftliche Studien 56), Munich/Berlin 1987.  
Schnell, H., *Ottobeuren. Kloster und Kirche* (Große Kunstführer 2, 7th revised and enlarged edition), Regensburg 1979.  
Wagner, H., *Barocke Festsäle in bayerischen Klöstern und Schlössern*, Munich 1974, pp. 112–6.  
Hitchcock, H.-R., *Rococo Architecture in Southern Germany*, London/New York 1968, pp. 198–201.
fd47a768-1c13-5b0f-82f0-572eb14c0584.history: Founded in 764 by a count of the name Silach an important historical turning point for the Lower Swabian Benedictine Monastery Ottobeuren was the appointment to a sovereign Imperial Abbey in the 13th century. The land over which this rule extended included a multitude of villages, which later would be the financial basis for the economic and cultural expansion that the monastery experienced during the first half of the 18th century under the active Abbot Rupert Ness. Addressed as the “Hereditary Imperial Chaplain”, Abbot Rupert attempted to express his political closeness to the imperial court in Vienna with an enormous residence-like monastery. This expensive complex, on which a legion of local and trans-local artists worked, was such a strain on the finances of the abbey that the church building had to be delayed. Shortly before his death, Abbot Rupert commissioned the Swabian master builder Simpert Kramer for the construction of the church; however, in 1743, his successor transferred this responsibility to the famous architect Johann Michael Fischer from Munich, who was able to complete the prestigious building in 1766.
fd47a768-1c13-5b0f-82f0-572eb14c0584.patrons: Abbots Rupert II Ness (gov. 1710–1740), Anselm Erb (gov. 1740–1767)
fd47a768-1c13-5b0f-82f0-572eb14c0584.architects:
Monastery complex (selection), architecture: Father Christoph Vogt OSB (1648–1725), Simpert Kramer (1675–1753), Andrea Maini (b. 1683); stucco, among others: Johann Baptist Zimmermann (1680–1758), Andrea Maini (b. 1683), Cristoforo Volpini (d. 1733); frescos in the Imperial Hall, its forecourt and south stairwell: Karl Jakob Stauder (1694–1751/56); frescoes of the Theatre Hall and north stairwell of the Imperial Hall: Franz Josef Spiegler (1691–1757); ceiling paintings of the Benedictus Chapel, the Winter Abbey and the Prince’s Rooms: Jacopo Amigoni (1682–1752)  
Abbey church (selection), architecture: Simpert Kramer (1675–1753), Johann Michael Fischer (1692–1766); frescoes: Johann Jakob (1708–1783), Franz Anton Zeiller (1716–83/94); stucco and altar architecture: Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772); sculpture and design of the choir stalls: Johann Joseph Christian (1706–1777); joinery of choir stalls and confessionals: Martin Hörmann (1688–1782)
keywords: Imperial abbey; monastery; Benedictine Order; Imperial Hall; ceremonial hall; theatre; high altar; font; ceiling painting
fd47a768-1c13-5b0f-82f0-572eb14c0584.author: Maximilian Aracena, Peter Heinrich Jahn

ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.name: *Navis nundinaria* (The trading ship)
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.alternate_name: A ship-shaped theatre for the roast pork feast of 1657
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.description:
The *Insignia degli Anziani Consoli*, bound in 16 volumes and housed in the Archivio di Stato Bologna, are documents on parchment. They were made every two months, from 1530 to 1796, to celebrate the eight Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere di Giustizia, a group of magistrates ruling the city. From the end of the sixteenth-century, the names of the magistrates were depicted flanked by their coats of arms and a significant event that had taken place during the two months of their charge: an extraordinary visual chronicle illustrating more than two centuries of the city's history with six pictures a year.  
This picture (IV bimester of 1657) shows the stage for the roast pork feast. Celebrated every year on the 24th of August, a special installation was ssembled on the main square to host the feast of St. Bartholomew. In 1657 the theatre was shaped as a ship and was occupying nearly all the square, between the palace of the Podestà on the left and the stairs of the basilica of St. Petronius on the right. Along the sides of the ship were the stalls for the feast of the Assumption (from 15th to 24th August) that were going to become on the 24th boxes for the paying audience watching a theatrical representation and taking part in the traditional distribution of roast pork. On the mast waves the flag of the Municipality, under it a standard shows the coats of arms of Pope Alexander VII among those of the cardinal legate and of the archbishop of Bologna. On the aft deck a tent hosts the nine coats of arms of the Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere of the bimester July-August 1657. On top right a Latin inscription in golden ink describes the picture and bears the names of the Anziani Consoli.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.short_description: This illumination represents a theatre in the shape of a ship that was built on the Main Square of Bologna for the feast of the roast pork in August 1657. This was an event that attracted a great number of people every year. The ship sails are the coats of arms of the nine families of the Anziani Consoli and the Gonfaloniere, who ruled Bologna in the bi-mester July-August 1657. On the left side of the ship, is the portico of the Palazzo del Podesta. In the background is the Pavaglione and the Palazzo dei Banchi.  The stairs on the right lead to the church of San Petronio.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.initial_owner: The Anziani Consoli of the town of Bologna
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.method_for_datation: The date and the names of the magistrates are inscribed on the top right of the picture.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.obtention: This illumination, like the whole series, has always been housed in the archive of the Bolognese senate, inside the municipal palace. It was transferred to the Archivio di Stato in 1874, when it was created.
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.bibliography:
Plessi, G. *Le Insignia degli Anziani del Comune dal 1530 al 1796. Catalogo-Inventario*, Rome, 1954.  
*Il Magnifico apparato. Pubbliche funzioni, feste e giuochi bolognesi nel Settecento* (exhibition catalogue) (ed. S. Camerini), Bologna, 1982.  
Matteucci, A. M. “La cultura dell'effimero a Bologna nel XVII secolo”, *Barocco Romano e Barocco Italiano. Il teatro, l'effimero, l'allegoria* (eds. M. Fagiolo and M. L. Madonna), Rome, 1985, pp. 159-173.  
Zanni Rosiello, I. “Le Insignia degli Anziani: un autoritratto celebrativo”, *Società e storia:* 52, 1991, pp. 329-362.  
Giansante, M. “Gerarchie e scenografie. La festa della porchetta nelle Insignia degli Anziani Consoli di Bologna”, *I quaderni del M.AE.S.:* 8, 2005, pp. 93-125.
keywords: Illumination; Coats of arms; feast; festival; fairs; theatre; scenography; ephemeral architecture; Gonfaloniere; heraldry; trade
ff18d270-eb9c-5402-a699-82117263e1b6.author: Massimo Giansante

005e90ce-6216-5bb3-85d1-0c7504f54f18.name: *The triumphal entrance of Pope Paul III in Bologna*
005e90ce-6216-5bb3-85d1-0c7504f54f18.description: The fresco shows the procession of cardinals and knights escorting Pope Paul III Farnese to the Municipal Palace – represented in details in the background – during his stay in Bologna in 1543, before his meeting with the emperor Charles V in Busseto.

01e1c817-734d-5515-87fd-10abc3d72ece.name: Electors’ box with coat-of-arms
01e1c817-734d-5515-87fd-10abc3d72ece.description: The voluminous Elector’s (royal) box, supported by Atlantes-herms, stands out due to its opulent decoration. The box is crowned by putti and the personification of Fama (Fame) as an allegory of glory, surrounding the monogram of Elector Max III Joseph.
01e1c817-734d-5515-87fd-10abc3d72ece.location: Above the entrance on a level with the first and second tiers opposite the stage
01e1c817-734d-5515-87fd-10abc3d72ece.artist: François de Cuvilliés the Elder (1695–1786); Johann Baptist Straub (1704–1784)

02c7cd31-a334-540d-862c-127ba23ad756.name: Triumphal Arch – detail
02c7cd31-a334-540d-862c-127ba23ad756.description: Basic shapes of the monument refer to Early Baroque architecture with elements of late Renaissance Classicism.

056db7b3-89b9-5e48-919c-5e2963c5f874.name: Royal crypt with crucifixion group
056db7b3-89b9-5e48-919c-5e2963c5f874.description: Following its demolition in 1677 the crypt chapel of the Prince of Görz-Tyrol was rebuilt and set into the floor of the church so as not to obstruct the view; only the expressive crucifixion group above the crypt altar projects into the space of the church. The masterful craftsmanship of the royal crypt is a major work of the sculptor Andreas Thamasch, a student of Thomas Schwanthaler.

086158b7-4dfb-51de-82de-73c1ff47b61f.name: *Assumption of the Virgin*
086158b7-4dfb-51de-82de-73c1ff47b61f.description: One of the first illusionist ceiling paintings in north Croatia, this is the work of the local painter, Blasius Grueber, whose naïve characters are typical of  the artist’s work. The charm and emotional impact of Grueber’s paintings is similar to that of local painters in Tyrol.

09ba891e-91e5-5442-9d3f-f13cb83f8280.name: Alcove
09ba891e-91e5-5442-9d3f-f13cb83f8280.description:
It was probably realised after 1704, surely before 1739, when it is mentioned in a biography dedicated to its author, the sculptor Giuseppe Mazza, here working together with the painter Ercole Graziani senior.  
Coming back from Venice, the artist was probably engaged by the Zaniboni family, owner of the palace, to create this superb nuptial bedroom lavishly decorated with stuccoes and sculptures (among them *Venus* and *Apollo,* allusive to abundance and fertility); every element contributes here to a very dynamic composition inspired by typically baroque concepts.

0ca8f01a-192f-5192-af7d-85d181189024.name: *St. Ignatius in Heavenly Glory*
0ca8f01a-192f-5192-af7d-85d181189024.description: For this painting, Garcia was inspired by the composition which Cirro Ferri (1634–1689) painted on the dome of the church St Agnese in Rome. Both works were based on the experience and compositional patterns of Pietro da Cortona (1596–1669).
0ca8f01a-192f-5192-af7d-85d181189024.location: Ceiling of the sanctuary, Jesuit Church of St Ignatius

0dbd6f4d-41ee-5eab-8782-2834ac28c4e6.name: Staircase
0dbd6f4d-41ee-5eab-8782-2834ac28c4e6.description: Passalacqua inventively reinterpreted the Roman town plan for use in Dubrovnik. With a convex–concave, axially conceived staircase space (in the axis of which is the entrance to the college) he created a deep scenic vista, with which in a distinctive Late Baroque manner, he integrated the Jesuit complex into the structure of the city. Extensive demolition of existing houses was necessary to accommodate the staircase and to widen the street for access. Thanks to Passalacqua’s staircase, the Jesuit complex in Dubrovnik is considered as the highest quality example of Baroque architecture and town planning on the Croatian Adriatic coast.
0dbd6f4d-41ee-5eab-8782-2834ac28c4e6.location: Jesuit Church of St Ignatius, college and Jesuit stairs

169326c2-920f-568e-865b-5feb37a401c0.name: Count’s Study
169326c2-920f-568e-865b-5feb37a401c0.description: The “Chinese” room was adjoined by a library. The floor, inlaid with several kinds of wood, was by the court joiner. The count consulted with the Viennese adviser, Conrad Adolph von Albrecht, who also worked for the Sinzendorfs in Židlochovice in most of his artistic activities.
169326c2-920f-568e-865b-5feb37a401c0.artist: Jacob Prandtauer (1660 Stanz – 1726 St. Pölten), Johann Friedrich Praetorius

177f9291-bc9c-5c91-b323-5a7e61e086be.name: *Urban II blessing the Bolognese Crusaders*
177f9291-bc9c-5c91-b323-5a7e61e086be.description: This scene shows the Pope blessing the Bolognese crusaders and their flags before the departure for the Holy Land for the First Crusade (October 1095). The representation, the clothing and the setting are in Baroque style.
177f9291-bc9c-5c91-b323-5a7e61e086be.artist: Giovanni Maria Bibiena (1625–1665) and Bartolomeo Morelli known as il Pianoro (dead 1703)

178756de-2fc7-5c0f-9aeb-af17d4b308f4.name: Diana, Goddess of the Hunt
178756de-2fc7-5c0f-9aeb-af17d4b308f4.description: In accordance with the use of the Amalienburg as a hunting lodge, the stuccoed overdoor of the main portal facing the garden depicts Diana, goddess of the hunt, as a half figure, surrounded with putti, hounds and hunting equipment.
178756de-2fc7-5c0f-9aeb-af17d4b308f4.location: Niche above the central portal of the eastern façade

18b9a5d2-56e7-5160-91ae-9a12388104ed.name: Monumental staircase; entrance
18b9a5d2-56e7-5160-91ae-9a12388104ed.description: Accessible from the atrium of the palace, the staircase is immediately visible thanks to its irregular and dynamic flight. The steps and balustrade immediately draw the sight and the attention of visitors.

1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.name: Electress’s Private Chapel
1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.description: Panelled with scagliola marble, the chapel flaunts its sumptuous ornamental decoration. To great effect, the ceiling, decorated with interlacing stuccowork, opens into an oval lantern displaying a fresco of heaven. The valuable altarpiece comes from the workshop of Peter Paul Rubens.
1b76ee67-59f5-5426-ae90-e4aff6200791.location: New Palace, first floor of the north wing

1b9bc4e6-e32d-5048-9385-04be938177c9.name: Monumental staircase
1b9bc4e6-e32d-5048-9385-04be938177c9.description: For this double flight staircase Pietro Canali was inspired by theatrical stage effects. Allegorical statues of *Hercules* and *Atlas* by Gabriele Brunelli (1615–1682) decorate the staircase. The vault was painted by Gioacchino Pizzoli (1651–1731).
1b9bc4e6-e32d-5048-9385-04be938177c9.artist: Pietro Canali; Gabriele Brunelli; Gioacchino Pizzoli

1d9489cb-b684-525a-aafd-7aef21007b06.name: *Allegory of Time*
1d9489cb-b684-525a-aafd-7aef21007b06.description: A superb example of “quadratura” by the celebrated Angelo Michele Colonna, a specialist in painted architectures. Giuseppe Alboresi painted the figures inside the large oval at the centre of the ceiling. The scene represents the *Allegory of Time driving away Venus and the Graces*.
1d9489cb-b684-525a-aafd-7aef21007b06.artist: Angelo Michele Colonna (1604–1687) and Giuseppe Alboresi (1632–1677)

2526f022-a75b-57ec-834d-4ab4413501d1.name: Chapel of the Holy Blood
2526f022-a75b-57ec-834d-4ab4413501d1.description: The medieval chapel annex was built before the monastery church in the Baroque style. Of special interest is the cupola structure with shallow tribune erected to replace the former apse. The quarter of the cross vault with chamfered corners and massive piers occupied by pilasters, form four large arcades with wide semicircular arches, which in turn support the cupola. The High Baroque design of the central space is derived from the type of crossing found in St. Peter’s in Rome (cf. Rattenberg).
2526f022-a75b-57ec-834d-4ab4413501d1.location: Chapel annex, southwest of the abbey church

25d59ad7-f146-5a66-b99c-640d389ce20d.name: Altar of St. Barbara
25d59ad7-f146-5a66-b99c-640d389ce20d.description: Like its match, the Altar of St. Joseph, it is framed with a *trompe\-l'œil* painting of luxurious drapery rather than architectural elements. The role of the structural parts, overtaken by decorative and figural motifs such as volutes and *putti*, makes for the altar's picturesque and extremely dynamic sculptural programme.
25d59ad7-f146-5a66-b99c-640d389ce20d.location: Along the southern side of the triumphal arch, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.name: Collateral Altarpiece
26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.description: Both collateral altarpieces are very similar, made of gilt carved wood  and flanked by pilasters decorated with acanthus leaves.
26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.location: Church interior, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy
26371767-cb3f-5ce5-9d43-eccf210c490a.artist: Frei José de Santo António Ferreira (active1764-66)

2e551a44-ed15-554e-b118-1f8beb1b9f7d.name: The Virgin Mary of Old Brno
2e551a44-ed15-554e-b118-1f8beb1b9f7d.description: This picture of the Virgin Mary is named after its second location. It was the palladium of Brno, a miraculous picture (Thaumaturga) of the Madonna and Child donated to the Augustinian Monastery in Brno by Emperor Charles IV. Members of major Moravian aristocratic families were traditionally wedded before the Thaumaturga. The reliquary, originally embedded in the child’s heart, makes up the clasp of the Madonna’s dress. Relief letters, gilded crowns with precious stones, and a chain come from the period of the picture’s coronation and its incorporation into the new altar. The image was credited with the salvation of Brno from the Swedish siege at the end of the Thirty Years’ War, as well as with healing properties and other miracles.

2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.name: Ceiling fresco of the Great Hall
2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.description: The ceiling fresco of the Great Hall was once the world’s largest. Illustrating the fight between Aeneas and Turnus for the hand of the king’s daughter Lavinia, Aeneas, it is sometimes said resembles the Elector Max II Emanuel. The use of a painted landscape background instead of *trompe-l’oeil* architectural decoration was novel at the time.
2eb1f102-370e-5a15-aa76-966aead4921b.location: New Palace, first floor of the central wing

2f3b7be6-81ba-55c8-a553-1e425e26df8b.name: Cupola painting of the crossing
2f3b7be6-81ba-55c8-a553-1e425e26df8b.description: The large, circular dome fresco is surrounded by four stucco cartouches with pictures of the evangelists that show the wonder of Whitsun and its meaning for the worldwide mission of the church. The architectural scenery of the step-platforms, balustrades and surrounding obelisks is typical of the art of *mise en scène* used for composing ceiling paintings.
2f3b7be6-81ba-55c8-a553-1e425e26df8b.location: Crossing vault of the abbey church

31a2ed6c-a768-5550-a180-6fecff19b3b0.name: Exterior, south façade
31a2ed6c-a768-5550-a180-6fecff19b3b0.description: Designed by Gumpp in 1754, the Hofgasse Wing was completed according to his plans by 1756. The centre of the wing is composed of a monumental portal projection in the form of a gabled triumphal arch encompassing all four storeys. It is only here that Johann Martin Gumpp’s façade conception has been realised completely in accordance with his ideas. The influence of his brother Georg Anton’s country house façade is evident. The ponderous Late Baroque style has been adjusted to contemporary taste with the addition of rocaille work on the windows.

31a85a61-1ef8-530b-8b89-bfb3cb6f169d.name: Memorial Chapel for Emperor Franz I
31a85a61-1ef8-530b-8b89-bfb3cb6f169d.description: On the order of Maria Theresa the room in which the emperor died in August 1765 was converted into a memorial chapel by Pacassi and an endowment for ladies of rank was founded in his honour. The hall, structured with pilasters, is adorned with gentle rocaille stucco of which the tribune features a painted relief group of God the Father with mourning angels from Franz Anton Leitensdorffer (1721–95).

34bb86f6-37dc-5242-9419-abe2436ed8e4.name: Stairway (general view)
34bb86f6-37dc-5242-9419-abe2436ed8e4.description: The design for the staircase was drawn up in 1777. Building began in 1781 and continued until 1969.
34bb86f6-37dc-5242-9419-abe2436ed8e4.location: Exterior, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy

3e274dad-a65b-5160-a9e1-d5f8cc5ac311.name: Monumental staircase
3e274dad-a65b-5160-a9e1-d5f8cc5ac311.description: Restored by the architect Francesco Tadolini, this staircase connecting ground and first-floor is decorated with architectural motives, typical of the so called ‘quadratura’ genre; this technique, based on very sophisticated perspective skills and strictly linked to the making of theatrical sceneries, was typical of the Bolognese school during baroque age. Their author, Pietro Scandellari, had been one of the first and most appreciated pupils of Ferdinando Galli, called Bibiena, who, together with his brother, sons and nephews, excelled in those fields all over Europe. The decoration is characterised by the opening of illusive views, which expand the space of the real architecture thanks to the virtual dimension of painting.

4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.name: Interior
4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.description: General view of the interior of the church. There is a huge representation of Calvary with life-size figures at the main altar.
4245f4f1-ced8-58b2-8737-09920f72fa22.location: Bom Jesus Church, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

432eb32a-5dbe-51f2-bd94-bbb4fc20e188.name: *King Francis I heals the People affected by Scrofula*
432eb32a-5dbe-51f2-bd94-bbb4fc20e188.description: In the Middle Ages people believed that the kings of France and England had a special power that could heal scrofula by just touching those afflicted with the illness. Here the king of France, Francis I, is shown healing the people affected by scrofula during his visit to Bologna in 1515.

43c6d616-3140-55ee-a6e8-3280cf935f70.name: Altar of the Birth of the Virgin Mary (high altar)
43c6d616-3140-55ee-a6e8-3280cf935f70.description: The high altar, Schmädl’s first large scale piece, is impressive due to its extensive architecture of grandiose column clusters and a canopy in the form of a drapery held by angels, with which the stage of a sacred act is architecturally framed in accordance with the Baroque Theatrum Sacrum. Including its uncommon three-dimensional representation of the birth of the Virgin Mary, the Rottenbuch example is designed according to the archetype represented by Egid Quirin Asam’s theatrically sculpted altars.

4538f38d-a64f-5f64-ba07-d2b5bab3e669.name: Riesensaal
4538f38d-a64f-5f64-ba07-d2b5bab3e669.description: The “Riesensaal”, whose name is derived from an earlier cycle of Hercules paintings, together with the court chapel, is the second room dedicated to the memory of Emperor Franz I and designed according to the model of the Grand Gallery in Schönbrunn Palace. The banqueting hall extending across the whole width of the wing on Rennweg encompasses two storeys and seven window axes. It is furnished in honour of the House of Habsburg. The huge fresco panels depict allegories, the oil paintings the family of the imperial couple.

46629869-175a-5ce1-8e92-45a1b32d5f70.name: Hall of the Ancestors
46629869-175a-5ce1-8e92-45a1b32d5f70.description: The wainscoting, a copy of the imperial office in Vienna, features family portraits by leading Viennese portraitists including J. Kupecký. The vaulting is decorated with the painting *The Celebration of Jaroměřice*, framed by illusionary architecture.
46629869-175a-5ce1-8e92-45a1b32d5f70.artist: Josef Emanuel Fischer von Erlach (1656–1742 Vienna?), Tobias Gravani, Johann Gotfried Auerbach, Johann Baptist Glunck, Martin Meytens (1695 Stockholm – 1770 Vienna), Domenico Maria Francia, Alessandro Ferretti

4692d873-94e6-59eb-9dc0-1830c1081690.name: Ceiling fresco
4692d873-94e6-59eb-9dc0-1830c1081690.description: Guglielmi’s high-grade ceiling fresco depicts allegories of the Four Continents but doesn’t leave any doubt about the supremacy of Europe. Again, the topic shows a clear connection to the life and work of the patron. In the centre of the painting stands Mercury, the god of trade, with a cornucopia. The theme is trade and its worldwide power spreading European comforts, announced by Fame, all over the world. The accentuated exotic design of the figures corresponds with the painted over-doors in the ballroom.

47ae5572-acbf-57a2-be11-0e35cf01e522.name: *The Glory of St. Ignatius of Loyola*
47ae5572-acbf-57a2-be11-0e35cf01e522.description: The glory of the founder saint of the Jesuits dominates the middle of the vault of the chapel. It is inspired by the great decoration with the same subject painted by Andrea Pozzo in Rome.
47ae5572-acbf-57a2-be11-0e35cf01e522.location: Chapel of the Jesuit novitiate, vault

4bdace62-bc43-503d-9780-29b787d8dbe1.name: Hall of Mirrors
4bdace62-bc43-503d-9780-29b787d8dbe1.description: As the heart of the small palace , the Hall of Mirrors functioned as a ballroom, concert hall or as a place of relaxation for the court society following a hunt. Mirrors inside the hall are applied to the wall sections between the windows. The interplay of real and reflecting windows appears to dissolve the surface of the walls and blurs the boundaries between the inside and the outside. The  windows and mirrors are framed with sophisticated Régence style décor and silver-plated carvings. Zimmermann's capriccio-like stuccoes of the ceiling transforms it into an Eden-like landscape by depicting trees, putti, divine figures and birds. This theme of the décor is used to connect the interior of the Amalienburg with its formerly surrounding French formal  garden.
4bdace62-bc43-503d-9780-29b787d8dbe1.artist: Design: François de Cuvilliés the Elder (1695–1768); Stucco: Johann Baptist Zimmermann (1680–1758); Ornamental carvings: Johann Joachim Dietrich (1690–1753)

50647a20-01f3-57bc-8f5f-7e46ecf4d6a4.name: Altar of St. Cross
50647a20-01f3-57bc-8f5f-7e46ecf4d6a4.description: The story of Redemption through the sacrifice of Christ is represented by burning souls behind the bars of the altar cavity; *Supper at Emaus,* modelled in low relief on the doors of the *tabernaculum*; the huge sculptures of St. Veronica and St. Barbara on either side; St. Mary, Mary Magdalen and St. Joseph standing in front of the painted *Crucifixion* and, finally, God surrounded by angels in the attic.
50647a20-01f3-57bc-8f5f-7e46ecf4d6a4.location: The Chapel of the Holy Cross

514d8dc0-868f-5204-a073-0bc44b2dabbb.name: Robillion Pavilion
514d8dc0-868f-5204-a073-0bc44b2dabbb.description: Designed by Robillion, the Pavilion is sometimes considered one of Portugal's first Neo-Classical buildings. However, it is no more than an expression of the *French* Baroque – obviously more “Classical” – attached to the overall palace form. It has two floors and a considerable monumentality, emphasised by the Stairway of the Lions.

528f12d4-5b9e-5f75-a717-5d6b25977d21.name: Pagan gods
528f12d4-5b9e-5f75-a717-5d6b25977d21.description: Although these are reminiscent of antique statues, the gods fit perfectly in the illusionistic architecture, painted by the artist to create artificial effects in order to amaze the visitors.

53a5bd73-a238-53c4-81c9-59518376497e.name: Coronation Monstrance
53a5bd73-a238-53c4-81c9-59518376497e.description: The radial monstrance is decorated with vine leaves and grapes, the Eucharist, symbol of Christ’s blood. Below the casket is a relief of the Madonna and Child; at the top, under a baldachin, is God and the dove of the Holy Spirit. Cartouches on the richly wrought pedestal feature paintings on enamel: the Madonna of Old Brno and half-figures of the order’s saints.

5545cb27-0785-507a-9024-c4b15d333e54.name: Monumental staircase; Statue of Sisyphus
5545cb27-0785-507a-9024-c4b15d333e54.description:
Sisyphus, the son of Aeolus and King of Corinth, is represented carrying a rock towards a mountain. This is the punishment he was condemned to after his death.  
His presence, should be considered along with Athena, the symbol of Learning in the niche above. This may be alluding to the struggle of the Human race for the conquest of Wisdom.
5545cb27-0785-507a-9024-c4b15d333e54.artist: Giovanni Carlo Sicinio Galli Bibiena (architect), Filippo Scandellari (sculptor), Giovan Battista Canepa (sculptor's aid)

564b795c-c024-5183-8ef7-83ea55c2e465.name: Christ Appears on the Sea of Galilee
564b795c-c024-5183-8ef7-83ea55c2e465.description: The cartouche is in the Rococo style. The central area, in low relief, presents the miraculous catch of fish described in the Gospel of St. John (21: 1–14).

5718ac81-d92d-51a8-a1ec-2e1b0253d7a9.name: Theatre room
5718ac81-d92d-51a8-a1ec-2e1b0253d7a9.description: The theatre room was used for the performance of spiritual enactments.
5718ac81-d92d-51a8-a1ec-2e1b0253d7a9.location: North wing (3rd floor), Benedictine Abbey of St. Theodor and Alexander

571b4393-48a0-5d36-b275-9a37e8ea9df6.name: Coronation Paraments
571b4393-48a0-5d36-b275-9a37e8ea9df6.description: Fabrics were essential elements of the coronation ceremony. Viennese embroiderers frequently worked for the monastery. In comparison with other preserved Paraments these appear rather poor. The most spectacular part of the coronation set was the altar with an altarpiece. Accompanying elements were subordinated to it through their reduced decorativeness.

57410af1-c860-5014-8639-e6bbd059adc1.name: *Felsina between Peace and War*
57410af1-c860-5014-8639-e6bbd059adc1.description: The fresco in the Audience Room (today the Fireplace Room) was painted by Marco Antonio Franceschini and  shows Felsina (Bologna's name in Latin) between War and Peace. The scene is framed by “quadrature” (architectural illusionistic paintings) by Enrico Haffner. Felsina is crowned with laurels by Fame, while below them a lion and a lamb represent the desire of peace.
57410af1-c860-5014-8639-e6bbd059adc1.location: Fireplace Room, first floor, Palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti

58dd5f59-71f0-5f4d-bc1e-ecd6fcdecdae.name: High Altar
58dd5f59-71f0-5f4d-bc1e-ecd6fcdecdae.description:
Sculptures of St. Peter and St. Paul, St Ignatius and St Frances Xavier standing in shallow niches furnish the lower side sections of the high altar. At either side of the retable are sculptures of *St. John Nepomuk* and *St. Donat Martyr*. In the attic, the *Annunciation* accompanied by saints and angels, is divided into two zones.  
In around 1737, the sculptor, Ivan Walz, was working in Varaždin having taken over the workshop of the Reiss-Schoy family in Maribor, thus it is probable that this altarpiece is his work.

5bab92c3-59a2-5508-84dd-c3ea097dc2d5.name: Façade
5bab92c3-59a2-5508-84dd-c3ea097dc2d5.description: Of Christoph Gumpp’s plans for a double-tower façade only the north tower was completed by 1667. The forebuilding in the form of a monumental portico was completed by Gumpp’s grandson, Georg Anton, under Abbot Gregor von Stremer. This High Baroque forebuilding of Roman monumentality opens at its centre to form a large niche framed by an aedicule. The statues of the legendary giants Haymon and Thyrsus, as well as the figures from the upper balustrade, are early, somewhat crude works from Nikolaus Moll.
5bab92c3-59a2-5508-84dd-c3ea097dc2d5.artist: Christoph Gumpp the younger (1600–1672); Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754); Nikolaus Moll (1676–1754)

5d384b4b-2125-59b9-a241-75c9c513995b.name: Stucco ornamentation
5d384b4b-2125-59b9-a241-75c9c513995b.description: The decoration consists of floral ornamentation, angels, and figurative representations depicting scenes from St Frances Xavier’s missionary activities and his dying vision on Shangchuan Island in China.
5d384b4b-2125-59b9-a241-75c9c513995b.location: The Chapel of St. Francis Xavier

5da28193-df85-5125-983e-01722d0be0e4.name: *The fall of Phaeton*
5da28193-df85-5125-983e-01722d0be0e4.description: Burrini is considered the most “baroque” Bolognese painter for his dynamic and fluid painting style. He represents the myth of Phaeton, who is falling down from the sky with his chariot and horses in a sort of vortex.

5dcb2629-41cc-5771-865e-799a7eb11951.name: Pulpit
5dcb2629-41cc-5771-865e-799a7eb11951.description: The basket and sounding board of the pulpit show a spirited moulding as was typical  of the era. Highly gesturally executed sculptures of the four evangelists are mounted in pairs to the basket, while at the very top, an angel with the commandment tablets establishes a typological reference to the Old Testament.

61326b88-96a4-5ced-9671-1bceca375464.name: The Saints in Heaven (so-called Heaven of Dießen)
61326b88-96a4-5ced-9671-1bceca375464.description:
In this dome fresco, innumerable saints and beatified persons from the various branches of the founding noble family, the Counts of Dießen-Andechs, form a group amassed around Christ. As being such, they exemplify the cardinal virtues which are depicted in the pendentives.  
Having been carefully calculated both narrationally and perspectively, the oldest locally revered members of the Dießen-Andechs family (Rasso, Rathard and Mechtildis) are the first to catch the eye of those entering the church.

6174afaa-9d22-5990-a88e-438c271eaecb.name: Trophy
6174afaa-9d22-5990-a88e-438c271eaecb.description: Four magnificent stucco trophies decorate the corners of the ballroom ceiling. They represent a unicorn head surrounded with arms and flags, creating an elegant composition.

638b8d0b-c143-5fcb-b7eb-99c572ca9cf5.name: Cartouche with inscription
638b8d0b-c143-5fcb-b7eb-99c572ca9cf5.location: Central part of the arch below the niche

68e9823a-426f-5c71-85b6-2202e4741be6.name: The Altar of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary (high altar)
68e9823a-426f-5c71-85b6-2202e4741be6.description: The grandiose high altar, measuring 14 x 20 metres, depicts the Assumption of the Virgin Mary into Heaven through the media of painting and sculpture. The altarpiece can be retracted, revealing interchangeable backdrops which are used to assist with the theatrical displaying of salvation history on different feast days. Four larger-than-life statues of the Church Fathers flank the high altar on both sides – truly they are crowning achievements of Bavarian Baroque sculpture on account of their solemn expressionalism.

6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.name: General view of the Stairway of the Five Senses and the Fountain of Vision  and of  Taste
6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.description: This stairway continues the theme of the hierarchy of the five senses, as if revealing in the ascending course the degree of corporeity that should be attributed to each of the senses. The mythological figures found at the axis of the fountain were re-“Christianised” by order of the Censorial Court in 1774 having previously been considered “indecorous” due to their proximity to the biblical figures. The figures – whose original denominations are well known – were maintained and only the inscriptions were changed.
6f0f07b0-eee8-503e-a5b8-02651b202a00.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

76936470-37f5-5740-97e3-6a78439dffef.name: Abbot’s Coronation Sceptre
76936470-37f5-5740-97e3-6a78439dffef.description: The spiral part of the sceptre is covered with acanthus leaves and multi-coloured cut glass. In the central halo there is an image of the Madonna of Old Brno transferred into relief form as a cast statue.

7b24d963-dbed-5062-9184-43967c49d4a8.name: Atrium
7b24d963-dbed-5062-9184-43967c49d4a8.description: Painted in the same style as the walls of the staircase, the atrium introducing to the main apartment on the first floor was originally decorated with sculptures, today missing.

7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.name: Fountain of the Five Holy Wounds
7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.description: The motto for the theme of the senses is given by the first fountain, which refers precisely to the Suffering of Christ, and presents the symbolism that summarises the *Via Crucis*: The Five Holy Wounds Fountain. The fountain tablet presents in relief the instruments of the Passion of Christ.
7d79aec6-af13-5110-a27e-45a7ec8a4d19.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga Sanctuary (Bom Jesus do Monte)

8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.name: *St. Stephen* (Altar of St. Stephen)
8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.description: The young deacon, Stephen, is shown in a scene of apotheosis, surrounded by a wreath of clouds and a halo.
8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.location: Central inter-columnation of the Altar of St Stephen (south chapel), Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow
8040d180-a30b-5c06-b882-58cee878370d.artist: Circle of the sculptor, Filip (Philipp) Jakob Straub (1706–1774)

81b4bb52-8b07-5a5b-88b7-ddd086e84db0.name: High altar
81b4bb52-8b07-5a5b-88b7-ddd086e84db0.description: The high altar with a height of almost 19 metres forms the focal point of the prospect which opens up when entering the church. As in a processional way, the sequence of altars leads to this central point. The altarpiece shows Mary as the Queen of the Rosary with the church’s two patrons. A special feature of the altar is the altar crown, a stage-like, perspectively designed Solomonic lion’s throne on which Christ is seated: “Ecce plus quam Salomon hic” (See more than Solomon). The statues (St. Augustine, Norbert as well as Vigilius and Cassian) were modified by Josef Stapf in 1768.
81b4bb52-8b07-5a5b-88b7-ddd086e84db0.dates: 1662–1665: ciborium; 1671: altar painting; 1768: modification of the mensa/statues
81b4bb52-8b07-5a5b-88b7-ddd086e84db0.location: East wall of the choir, Catholic Collegiate Church of St. Lawrence and St. Stephen
81b4bb52-8b07-5a5b-88b7-ddd086e84db0.artist: Paul Huber [n.d.]; Josef Stapf [n.d.], Ferdinand Fries [n.d.]; Johann (Hans) Schor (1615–1674); Egid Schor (1627–1701)

89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.name: The *Baptism of Christ*
89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.description: The Baptism group, conceived as a counterpart to the pulpit, belongs among the major works of Swabian Rococo for, among other reasons, the sensitive gestures of the sculptures and the capricious form of the altar-like framing.
89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.location: Northeast crossing pillar of the abbey church, above the baptismal font
89f1df55-2357-58fe-bc86-45fa395f58bf.artist: Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772); Johann Joseph Christian (1706–1777)

8e028480-2139-5321-be75-aa5ace6155c1.name: The boxes
8e028480-2139-5321-be75-aa5ace6155c1.description: The boxes are supported by mermaids and caryatids all represented in different attitudes.
8e028480-2139-5321-be75-aa5ace6155c1.artist: Bolognese sculptors, probably Camporesi or Balugani

8ef6164d-8b25-56fd-9a75-9a922be66c14.name: Mass Chalice and Jugs
8ef6164d-8b25-56fd-9a75-9a922be66c14.description: Apart from the chalice decorated with half-figures of the order’s saints painted on enamel, and jugs for Abbot Zirckl, there were two other chalices for assisting priests, with scenes from the Lfe and Torment of St. John of Nepomuk and the Passion, created in the Augsburg workshop for the coronation.

8f913dd6-44f7-5383-a80c-856aa602cf61.name: Interior, facing east
8f913dd6-44f7-5383-a80c-856aa602cf61.description: The spatial image, dominated by the Early Baroque fittings, is divided into two zones, a lower with side chapels and altars and an upper with choir lofts and vault, which are characterised by the bold, heavy stucco and the colourful fresco panels. The altars are arranged according to the strict Early Baroque aedicula scheme and are all framed in black and gold. The high altar with its triumphal altar crown forms the connection between the two zones. The indirect light falling on chapels and choir lofts plays a decisive role in generating the atmosphere of a scared theatre.
8f913dd6-44f7-5383-a80c-856aa602cf61.location: Catholic Collegiate Church of St. Lawrence and St. Stephen
8f913dd6-44f7-5383-a80c-856aa602cf61.artist: Christoph Gumpp the younger (1600–1672); Bernardo Pasquale [n.d.]; Kaspar Waldmann (1657–1720)

8fe0581a-5b87-5ce5-b038-f57ad44a0666.name: The Re-establishment of the Dießen monastery by the Counts of Andechs
8fe0581a-5b87-5ce5-b038-f57ad44a0666.description:
Contrary to custom, it is not St. Augustine, the founder of the order of the Augustinian Canons, who dominates the series of frescos, but rather the history of the Dießen monastery itself. This was done to remind the House of Wittelbach as contemporary rulers of Bavaria of its responsibility to care for the monastery as the legal successors of the founding family which had died out in the Middle Ages.  
The main fresco recalls the re-establishment of the former double monastery by Count Berthold II of Andechs in this way: Under celestial auspices, papal confirmation is given to the men’s convent of St. Mary in 1132 against the backdrop of the Lateran Palace in Rome. On the other side, the admission of Mechtildis, the Count’s juvenile daughter, into the short-lived women’s convent of St. Stephen in 1139 is depicted against an imagined backdrop of the medieval local monastery church, typologically referring to Mary’s entrance into the Temple.

9d1b3ddb-6a64-5dc1-ae7b-afa6d1da6b9b.name: Exterior, east façade
9d1b3ddb-6a64-5dc1-ae7b-afa6d1da6b9b.description: The Hofburg’s main façade differs significantly from that facing the Hofgasse. The wing was erected between 1766–80 according to plans from Pacassi and under the direction of the Viennese military architect Constantin Walter von Pfeilsberg. Gumpp’s plan was abandoned in favour of a new conception. The elongated, lightly curved front is designed along the lines of the Viennese palace built at the same time. It has a high basement storey and colossal order, with two seven-axis portal projections and rounded corner pavilions composed of existing towers.

9e276d65-268c-5885-a7c1-1b671be8c8e8.name: View of the sanctuary
9e276d65-268c-5885-a7c1-1b671be8c8e8.description: The architect of the Church of St. Ignatius in Dubrovnik, Andrea Pozzo, envisaged a fresco painting for the sanctuary, dividing it with pillars into three parts – as he had done in his own painting in the church of the same name in Rome – and setting the iconographical programme. The programme was perceived as the *Apotheosis of the Work of St. Ignatius* in the central field of the sanctuary, the *Encounter of St. Ignatius with St. Francis Xavier and St. Francis Borgia* in the side fields and *St. Ignatius in Heavenly Glory* on the ceiling of the sanctuary. The wall paintings were executed by the Sicilian painter of Spanish descent (who trained in Rome and Naples), Gaetano Garcia. Looking to show case patterns from Rome, like Pozzo's St. Ignatius and the Church of St. Agnese in Agone (with dome frescos painted by Carlo Ferri), Garcia achieved an impressive High Baroque composition, with a pronounced dynamic, opulent colouring and an effective play of light and shadow. The largest Baroque fresco cycle in Dalmatia, it gives some inkling of the splendour intended for the interior of the Dubrovnik Jesuit church, had the painting programme – which probably included the ceiling of the nave – been carried out to the end.
9e276d65-268c-5885-a7c1-1b671be8c8e8.location: Walls and ceiling of the sanctuary, Jesuit Church of St Ignatius

9f686f76-730a-5310-83dc-4ed16a53c99a.name: Proscenium
9f686f76-730a-5310-83dc-4ed16a53c99a.description: The facade-like arch-shaped structure near the front of the stage is supported by two colossal columns either side with the proscenium boxes between them. Above the centre of the stage the crest of the alliance of Bavaria–Saxony is prominently displayed.

a079adb4-175d-5bd2-96ab-5385a891031d.name: Herm pair: Autumn
a079adb4-175d-5bd2-96ab-5385a891031d.description: The herm pairs allegorise the seasons, this one showing an allegory of autumn.
a079adb4-175d-5bd2-96ab-5385a891031d.artist: François de Cuvilliés the Elder (1695–1786); Johann Baptist Straub (1704–1784)

aad909a1-b106-56bf-86ee-b7aee4a41eef.name: Central ceiling fresco in the Riesensaal
aad909a1-b106-56bf-86ee-b7aee4a41eef.description: The painted ceiling, including the painted stucco, covers an area of c. 500 square metres and is one of Franz Anton Maulbertsch’s major works. The empress personally contributed to its design. The central fresco shows an allegory of the union of the royal houses of Austria and Lorraine, the flanking ovals depict the regalia of Tyrol. The marriage of the houses of Austria and Lorraine is depicted as a chariot, accompanied by personifications of the sovereign’s virtues.

acbcd2fe-73a5-5680-ae25-a6b4c595a3b1.name: *Sala Terrena*
acbcd2fe-73a5-5680-ae25-a6b4c595a3b1.description: The space is decorated with illusionary ornamental painting evoking an overgrown pergola. The adjoining lounge contains Japanese genre scenes and “Roman” baths with stucco ornamentation decorated with shells and stones.
acbcd2fe-73a5-5680-ae25-a6b4c595a3b1.artist: Giovanni Michele Fontana, Johann Wenzl Bergl?

af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.name: High Altar
af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.description: Built thanks to the generosity of Viceroy Baltazar Bedeković and his wife, Helena Rozalija Somogy, the main altar's massive construction meets the full width and height of the sanctuary. According to the inscription on the cartouche at the top of the retable the altar was completed in 1743, although the sculpture of *Immaculate Mary* at the centre belonged to the old dismantled main altar made in 1729.
af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.location: Presbytery, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow
af670ccd-204f-5459-abf8-9e8b73bfa098.artist: Circle of the sculptor  Filip (Philipp) Jakob Straub (1706–1774)

afa63df6-92d1-5fda-adee-1fb5ac15e24c.name: High altar
afa63df6-92d1-5fda-adee-1fb5ac15e24c.description: The Early Baroque high altar built for the medieval monastery church by the sculptor Steinle from Weilheim is of special art-historical significance. The altar screen, architecturally formed by two columns, is overgrown with thick tendrils, a “Root of Jesse” or “Tree of Life”, springing from the base of the altar with the figures of Adam and Eve ascends via the central figure of the salvational “Immaculata” to the crucifixion as a symbol of redemption. The tradition of Late Gothic branch-motif ornamentation is here combined with Early Baroque forms. Stucco curtain and baldachin from Franz Xaver Feichtmayr added in 1731.
afa63df6-92d1-5fda-adee-1fb5ac15e24c.artist: Bartholomäus Steinle (c. 1580–1628/29); carpentry by Wolfgang Kirchmayr (dates unknown, working up until 1600)

b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.name: Victory Hall
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.description: The Regency-style panelled hall shows in its paintings, reliefs, concave moulding and ceiling fresco scenes of war, which refer to the Elector’s military success in the Turkish Wars. Scenes of the unsuccessful War of the Spanish Succession were deliberately avoided.
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.location: New Palace, first floor of the central wing
b7aa2d97-f660-5f39-a7c3-53ec68eec878.artist: Johann Adam Pichler (c. 1690–1761); Charles Dubut (c. 1687–1742): Jacopo Amigoni (c. 1682–1752); Joachim Beich (1665–1748)

b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.name: Throne Room
b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.description: The Throne Room, also known as the Great Room, is the largest of the palace's three state rooms. Construction began in 1768 when the marriage of Dom Pedro to the future Queen Maria I demanded a large area for official audiences. Designed by the architect, Jean-Baptiste Robillion, the new room was built in the Rococo style with carvings by the sculptor and wood carver, Silvestre de Faria Lobo. The paintings on the ceiling represent Faith, Sun, Hope, War, Justice and Charity and were executed under the direction of the painter, João de Freitas Leitão. Manuel da Costa, António Berardi and Manuel do Nascimento assisted him.
b9abc8a0-1fc1-59ad-9b41-3194b57afd27.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782); carving: Silvestre de Faria Lobo; painters: João de Freitas Leitão, Manuel da Costa, António Berardi, Manuel do Nascimento, whose dates are unknown.

bad50899-194a-53f5-8b17-f81567ff0b42.name: High altar
bad50899-194a-53f5-8b17-f81567ff0b42.description: The bundle of columns of the powerful main altar made of stucco marble forms an imposing frame for the topics of the altarpiece, namely the Trinity and Redemption. To the sides, larger-than-life stucco figures of the apostles Peter and Paul in ecstatically-moved depictions admonish the faithful, while respectively, the painting reflects on the secret of faith. On either side are the figures of the holy bishops Ulrich and Conrad, both of whom were patrons of the Swabian bishoprics of Augsburg and Konstanz.
bad50899-194a-53f5-8b17-f81567ff0b42.artist: Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772); Johann Joseph Christian (1706–1777); Johann Jakob Zeiller (1708–1783)

bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.name: Ceiling fresco of the Dining Room
bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.description: The enchanting fresco on the ceiling of the Dining Room shows Odysseus’ arrival at the nymph Calypso’s island guarded in heaven by gods. It was painted primarily during the reign of Max III Joseph.
bbb068e0-786d-5185-ae89-0a937e547d94.location: New Palace, ground floor of the central wing

bd83431f-3b68-50c1-b369-a3b63fc107e1.name: Staircase
bd83431f-3b68-50c1-b369-a3b63fc107e1.description: A two-shouldered staircase with stucco decoration is overlooked by a ceiling painting of *The Fall of the Titans*. A number of Italian artists who had settled in Vienna worked for Count Questenberk in the 1720s and 30s.

be223737-7c12-50b0-a7e8-cdae4ef617f5.name: Staircase
be223737-7c12-50b0-a7e8-cdae4ef617f5.description: Monti designed a so-called “macchina per salire” (machine to  ascend) that transformed the loggia into a theatrical stage, with stuccos by Carlo Nessi. The staircase consist of two symmetrical and opposite flights where the windows are open on illusionistic perspectives.
be223737-7c12-50b0-a7e8-cdae4ef617f5.location: Hall, ground floor, Palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti

beb103e2-c3d8-5595-a211-c4be2ed2c8ce.name: Bernhardisaal (Fürstensaal)
beb103e2-c3d8-5595-a211-c4be2ed2c8ce.description: Architecturally, the Bernhardisaal, extending over two storeys, is a simple rectangular room whose distinguishing feature is a rectangular opening in the ceiling with perimeter balustrade, a “hypaethral space” which gives the illusion of an opening onto heaven. It is the wall and ceiling paintings, covering the entire surface, that first turn the room into a ceremonial hall. A sequence of scenes from the life of the founder of the order, St. Bernhard of Clairvaux, culminates in the Christmas vision above the ceiling opening.
beb103e2-c3d8-5595-a211-c4be2ed2c8ce.location: Central pavilion of the western monastery wing, the so called “Bernhardibau”, Cistercian Monastery of Stams
beb103e2-c3d8-5595-a211-c4be2ed2c8ce.artist: Johann Martin Gumpp the elder (1643–1729) and Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754); Franz Michael Hueber (?–1746), Anton Zoller (1695–1768)

bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.name: Gardens
bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.description: Expansion of the garden was possible after resolution of the uneven land quotas and the relatively rough excavation. The garden's first designer was the Dutchman, Jan van der Kolke, who followed the plans of Robillion. The expansion followed a structure typical of the Portuguese “farm”, purchasing the surrounding land to create a formal garden, a recreational garden and a large area for cultivation, the *Quinta Real*.
bf8d5dd6-621c-537a-a14f-13c5c7464cea.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782); Garden statues: John Cheere (1709-1787)

c1efc606-bb1a-5e6b-a789-0a668d5179a7.name: Interior of the church
c1efc606-bb1a-5e6b-a789-0a668d5179a7.description: High Baroque longitudinal single-nave type with lateral chapels and dominant sanctuary

c2a04a59-d483-5172-86bf-965cfc076d63.name: Side altars depicting St. Stephen and St. Sebastian
c2a04a59-d483-5172-86bf-965cfc076d63.description:
As imports of Venetian painting, the pictures on the two middle altars embody the cosmopolitan taste of the Provost, Herculan Karg. Giovanni Pittoni painted the Protomartyr Stephen. Likewise, Giovanni Tiepolo, Pittoni’s even more renowned colleague, painted St. Sebastian who is the patron saint of plague victims.  
By intentionally eschewing the typical retable architecture, the sumptuous altarpieces appear to the viewer as being pictures in a gallery, unveiled by puttos through means of sculpted drapery which seems to be pulled aside. The flanking sculptures belong to a cycle depicting the 12 Apostles who are distributed among the side altars.
c2a04a59-d483-5172-86bf-965cfc076d63.location: The third pair of altars from the chancel. St. Stephen is on the left and St. Sebastian on the right.
c2a04a59-d483-5172-86bf-965cfc076d63.artist: Architecture and sculpture on the altars: Johann Baptist Straub (1704–84);  Altarpieces: Giovanni Battista Pittoni (1687–1767) and Giovanni Battista Tiepolo (1696–1770)

c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.name: Examples of *Via Crucis* chapels: Chapel of the Flagellation and the Mercury Fountain; Chapel of the Crucifixion and the interior of the Chapel of the Falls
c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.description: The Stairway of the Five Senses leads up to the Crucifixion Chapel. On the way up are other chapels one of which, the Chapel of the Flagellation, reinforces the Suffering of Christ or the *Via Crucis* as an element of purification.
c2fa115e-3ff1-53bd-a4fb-c6aa6c675900.location: The Stairway of the Five Senses, Bom Jesus de Braga (Bom Jesus do Monte)

c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.name: Ceremonial Façade (main façade)
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.description: Perhaps one of the best palace façades of the Portuguese Baroque, it combines traditional Portuguese features with Classical precision. The triangular pediment, adorned at the tympanum with garlands, averts the solemnity of a façade which is the keynote of the garden views.
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.location: Exterior view from the Pênsil Garden
c4949ddb-d9d5-551d-b5df-1849fe2e8307.artist: Jean Baptiste Robillion (active 1758–1782), Mateus Vicente de Oliveira (1706–1786)

c808701e-fb13-501f-b5ef-7e36dad27a4e.name: Pulpit
c808701e-fb13-501f-b5ef-7e36dad27a4e.description: A creative reinterpretation of the pulpit by J. B. Straub of 10 years earlier, it stands out in the pantheon of Baroque sculpture in northern Croatia at a time when sculpture and imaginatively and skilfully executed ornamental work were on the threshold of the Rococo.
c808701e-fb13-501f-b5ef-7e36dad27a4e.location: North side of the nave, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

c84f6b86-bda2-5650-b91c-dba0814eb447.name: Remedy Fountain
c84f6b86-bda2-5650-b91c-dba0814eb447.description: Situated in the centre of the Courtyard of the Kings, overlooking the staircase, is an obelisk fountain known as the Remedy Fountain. The obelisk in the centre of the fountain is 14 metres high.
c84f6b86-bda2-5650-b91c-dba0814eb447.location: Courtyard of the Kings, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy

c997623c-dc1e-5f87-b598-a6ef85003af7.name: Coronation of the Virgin Mary
c997623c-dc1e-5f87-b598-a6ef85003af7.description: The scene depicting the Coronation of the Virgin Mary with its plethora of figures was executed with little regard to viewing from below. Within a quatrefoil-shaped frame a series of picture levels are differentiated, ascending in sequence to the holy spirit in the form of a dove in an aureole, however this would also be clear when viewed frontally. In this case no effort has been made to create an impression of space or an imaginary heavenly opening when viewed from below using exaggerated perspective effects. Instead, traditional pictorial techniques have been employed.

cee30618-4395-58d9-9364-6ae0526dbf95.name: Church of St. Margaret
cee30618-4395-58d9-9364-6ae0526dbf95.description: The church, with an oval nave, presbytery and vestibule, is 20.2 m long, 14.8 m wide and 44 m high. Its fresco decoration is the apotheosis of St. Margaret. She is accompanied by two angels, crypto-portraits of the investor and his wife, Marie Antonie of Friedberg–Scheer. The nave contains six side altars. The two front altars feature reliquaries of two young martyrs, Saints Vincent and Reparata, presented by Pope Innocent XII to the count during his journey to Rome. The church joined the chateau and the area below it. The concept is not only of architectural importance but also manifests the connection between the sovereign and the people, considered an aspect of “beneficent reign”.
cee30618-4395-58d9-9364-6ae0526dbf95.artist: Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt (1668 Genoa – 1745 Vienna), František Antonín Findt, Karel František Tepper (1682–1738), Kaspar Ober

d0ab1550-cbd5-5935-b8c4-fe0633742da9.name: Neptune Fountain
d0ab1550-cbd5-5935-b8c4-fe0633742da9.description: The Neptune Fountain is perhaps one of the most remarkable pieces of 17th-century Baroque stonework in Portugal. Originating during the period of the Castelo Melhor, the fountain was commissioned in Rome shortly after 1675 , 1675 by Luis de Meneses, Count of Ericeira and Portuguese Ambassador in Rome, and made specifically for his Lisbon palace of Anunciada where it was installed in the gardens. After the earthquake of 1755, the fountain fell into the hands of other owners and ended up in several different locations. It was finally purchased by the state and placed in the gardens of Queluz in the first half of the 20th century. Today we know it was probably commissioned from Gian Lorenzo Bernini (the *“vernino*” as he is referred to in Portuguese documentation) who delegated work on it to Ercole Ferrata.

d554971f-f508-52e4-999c-e09207ee45b2.name: Ceiling of the Galleria del Senato
d554971f-f508-52e4-999c-e09207ee45b2.description: The personification of Bologna is standing on a chariot pulled by two lions, which symbolize the power of the City. She is guided by Cybele, the goddess of nature, to the glory of Olympus, where Jupiter welcomes her.

d6b2cb6a-1495-5fd3-9836-145bd04a8474.name: Frescos and stucco
d6b2cb6a-1495-5fd3-9836-145bd04a8474.description: The High Baroque interior work significantly changed the original spatial impression. In the vault the bay borders were masked with overlapping stucco and the introduction of colourful ceiling pictures in small panels provided a contrast to the Early Baroque colour scheme of white, gold and black. The vault’s heavenly zone is characterised by stucco putti, garlands of fruit and acanthus vine, the series of pictures depict, amongst other things, scenes from the life of the Virgin Mary (choir) and the Church patrons (nave).

d91086bf-1c10-54ef-9ee9-fd787e402072.name: Pagan gods
d91086bf-1c10-54ef-9ee9-fd787e402072.description: Although these are reminiscent of antique statues, the gods fit perfectly in the illusionistic architecture, painted by the artist to create artificial effects in order to amaze the visitors.

da426277-fa80-5d6b-bf9e-deb7c0f1f1c4.name: Detail of the alcove, putto
da426277-fa80-5d6b-bf9e-deb7c0f1f1c4.description:
It was probably realised after 1704, surely before 1739, when it is mentioned in a biography dedicated to its author, the sculptor Giuseppe Mazza, here working together with the painter Ercole Graziani senior.  
Coming back from Venice, the artist was probably engaged by the Zaniboni family, owner of the palace, to create this superb nuptial bedroom lavishly decorated with stuccoes and sculptures (among them *Venus* and *Apollo,* allusive to abundance and fertility); every element contributes here to a very dynamic composition inspired by typically baroque concepts.

dcb4b1e9-8570-58ec-bfd9-2967dc807b70.name: Ballroom with frescoes
dcb4b1e9-8570-58ec-bfd9-2967dc807b70.description:
The most famous fresco of the palace is that of the ballroom located on the the first floor, it represents the *Apotheosis of Marescotti's family* and was painted  by Giuseppe and Antonio Rolli. It shows  Wisdom, with  Glory on her left,  holding up a pyramid. The circle on the pyramid symbolizes eternity. The main scene is surrounded by oval medaillons with allegorical figures of cities connected with the Marescottis (Bologna, Rome, Siena) and the personification of Scotland.  
The family portraits on the walls were painted in 1709 by Giovanni Battista Caccioli.
dcb4b1e9-8570-58ec-bfd9-2967dc807b70.location: Salone Marescotti, first floor, Palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti
dcb4b1e9-8570-58ec-bfd9-2967dc807b70.artist: Giuseppe Rolli; Antonio Rolli; Giovanni Battista Caccioli

de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.name: Church Façade
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.description: The late 18th-century Rococo façade is divided into three parts, separated by Corinthian pilasters with capitals, and surmounted by a magnificent pediment built in the 19th century. The two towers, designed in 1848, were completed at the beginning of the 20th century. The pediment dates to around 1890. The first section of the stairway can also be seen in the photograph.
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.dates: c. 1750; towers: 1848; final design façade: 1880; pediment: c.1890
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.location: Exterior, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy
de217671-b0c6-5d52-a68e-4da53f3ccb53.artist: Church: António Mendes Coutinho (active 1750 ); stairs: Manuel Faustino Loureiro (active1782); Towers: Augusto de Matos Cid (active1880).

e0deac61-1689-5102-865c-bbe744a184c6.name: Death of St. Augustine in Hippo
e0deac61-1689-5102-865c-bbe744a184c6.description: The main fresco extends across two bays and is highlighted by a golden stucco frame. Matthäus Günther aesthetically contrasts the horrors of the Siege of Hippo by the Vandals to Augustine’s immensely towering deathbed and his ascent into heavenly glory as a theme of redemption. The artist obviously immortalises himself as the chronicler in the painting.

e1205084-57bd-571b-9800-802c7784d032.name: *The Coronation of the Emperor Charles V*
e1205084-57bd-571b-9800-802c7784d032.description: This scene documents one of the most important episodes in the history of Bologna and Europe: Pope Clement VII crowning Emperor Charles V in 1530. The sumptuous ceremony took place in Bologna in the church of San Petronio, facing the main square, next to the Municipal Palace.

e2f80c3c-ab05-5f27-aeeb-0c7c30fb8fa9.name: Stucco and ceiling paintings
e2f80c3c-ab05-5f27-aeeb-0c7c30fb8fa9.description: During the course of the Baroque redesign of the monastery church, which was vaulted between 1607 and 1609, ceiling pictures and stucco were also added to the nave and choir. The picture cycle in accordance with the preferences of the order, depict Marian themes as well as the life of the order’s founder. They are the work of the fresco artist Wolcker from Augsburg which is characterised by audacious illusionistic architecture. The stuccowork of the Wessobrun school is in the late strapwork style, at the transition to Rococo.
e2f80c3c-ab05-5f27-aeeb-0c7c30fb8fa9.artist: Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754, attributed to); Johann Georg Wolcker (1700–1766); Franz Xaver Feichtmayr the elder (1698–1763), Joseph Fischer [n.d.]

e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.name: Imperial Hall
e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.description: The architectonic and artificial painting arrangement of the ceremonial hall celebrates the idea and dignity of the Holy Roman Empire as well as the fidelity to the empire and the potential sovereignty of the abbey. The ceiling fresco shows the Coronation of Emperor Charlemagne in 800; four pictures to the sides describe the empire's functions in relation to its services for the church: *Ecclesiae propagatori* (propagator of the Church), *Ecclesiae propugnatori* (defender of the Church), *Hostium debellatori* (combatant against enemies) and *Scientiae fautori* (patron of science). Larger-than-life statues of the last 16 emperors, placed in front of the pompous columns of the wall decoration, show respectful reverence to the ruling House of Habsburg.
e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.location: Central projection of the west wing (3rd floor), Benedictine Abbey of St. Theodor and Alexander
e83f959c-c5a5-5804-9244-9b13dbf232e5.artist: Andrea Maini (b. 1683); Jakob Karl Stauder (1694–1751/56); Franz Anton Sturm (1690–1757)

e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.name: Bom Jesus Church
e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.description: At ground level there are two sculptural figures of the prophets, Jeremiah and Isaiah. Over the cornice, on the upper section, are the four evangelists.
e8770573-d328-5834-b1d9-a0c8ce5da0f6.location: Façade of the church in the Neo-Classical style, Bom Jesus de Braga (Bom Jesus do Monte)

ed6f3189-e588-5b12-a94c-6f71f36b6d21.name: Hercules
ed6f3189-e588-5b12-a94c-6f71f36b6d21.description: Although these figures are reminiscent of antique statues, the gods fit perfectly in the illusionistic architecture, painted by the artist to create artificial effects in order to amaze the visitors.

ee0459a7-7135-59f3-8a2f-96ace2250f9f.name: Ceiling fresco
ee0459a7-7135-59f3-8a2f-96ace2250f9f.description: Already on the staircase, the profession, rank and claim to power of von Liebenhofen are demonstrated. The ceiling is decorated with an oval fresco by Guglielmi, framed within gold-plated stucco. Its theme is the benefices of trade for the arts and sciences.

eea8e4f8-9634-582d-b793-e4253daa1b61.name: *Our Lady of Snow with Donors*
eea8e4f8-9634-582d-b793-e4253daa1b61.description: In the painted medallion are the kneeling figures of Adam Najšić, the chief notary of the Banovina of Croatia, and his wife, both of whom were donors of the church. Above them, on a cloud, sits Mary of the Snow with Christ on her lap. Below her, in the centre of the composition created as a skilful *trompe**\-**l'œil*, is the Roman Church of Santa Maria Maggiore in outline.
eea8e4f8-9634-582d-b793-e4253daa1b61.location: Ceiling, Parish Church of Our Lady of the Snow

ef57f78a-4a61-572b-9295-1a1a823103d5.name: Ballroom
ef57f78a-4a61-572b-9295-1a1a823103d5.description: This great hall is considered one of the most peculiar interiors in Italian Baroque architecture. It is a triple volume hall with several balustrades, culminating with the lantern on the top (33 m. height and about 800 square feet surface). There is no painted decoration, only white stucco mouldings that emphasise the extreme lightness of the architecture.

ef97269c-7f1c-524a-b766-0796d7d80956.name: *Apotheosis of the Work of St. Ignatius*
ef97269c-7f1c-524a-b766-0796d7d80956.description: The central figure of St. Ignatius is painted most probably after a print depicting the marble statue of the saint made by Camillo and Giuseppe Rusconi in 1733 for the Basilica of St. Peter’s in Rome.

fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.name: Main Altarpiece
fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.description: The Main altarpiece is decorated with gilded wood carving in the Rococo style, similar to that of Tibães Monastery, although adapted to a narrower space. The entire structure is elevated. Five steps lead up to the throne occupied by the image of Our Lady that is under a baldachin.
fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.location: Church Interior, Chancel, Sanctuary of Our Lady of Good Remedy
fa0f2509-a770-50de-bf2a-adc4110e9d91.artist: Frei José de Santo António Ferreira (act.1764–66), Luís Manuel da Silva (act.1766)
